candidate_relations.reason: Lymphocytic choriomeningitis does not represent the documented HTNV and SARS-CoV-2 coinfection.
Elevated renal markers support acute kidney injury, but AKI is a manifestation and omits both infectious components of the required coinfection diagnosis.
The record supports HTNV and SARS-CoV-2 by positive testing, not Ebola virus disease.
Severe leptospirosis can resemble HFRS clinically but is not the documented HTNV and SARS-CoV-2 coinfection.
Typhoid fever does not account for the specifically documented HTNV and SARS-CoV-2 coinfection.
Dengue may cause fever and thrombocytopenia but is not equivalent to the test-supported HTNV and SARS-CoV-2 coinfection.
